Title: After hours
Summary: A family home. An electricity bill that keeps rising.
Brief: The family says nothing has changed, but their electricity bill has risen. Examine the house and find three major sources of wasted energy. You have six detailed inspections.

Appliances.Name: Refrigerator
Appliances.Observation: The compressor seems to run often.
Appliances.Evidence: The gasket does not meet the frame. The family added a bulky food container five days ago; the compressor now runs much longer.

Actions.Text: Clear the obstruction and close the door
Disconnect the refrigerator with food inside

History: Five days ago / a large food container was added.
Yesterday / compressor active for 20 hours; previous average: 12 hours.
At inspection / cool air is escaping through the door gap.

Appliances.PreInspectionHint: The door looks almost closed, but one corner sits slightly proud of the frame. The motor remains audible while you look around.

Appliances.Name: Electric oven
Appliances.Observation: The oven is still warm after dinner.
Appliances.Evidence: Cooking finishes at 19:00. The oven stays on until 20:00 with no food inside. The household does this every evening.

Actions.Text: Switch it off when cooking is finished

Usage.OperatingTime: 2 h/day; only 1 h used for cooking
History: 20:00 / resident notices the indicator and switches it off.

Appliances.PreInspectionHint: The food has already been served, yet the heating indicator glows again. The family seems unsure who last touched the controls.

Appliances.Name: Desktop computer
Appliances.Observation: The study is empty, but the screen is on.
Appliances.Evidence: The resident works from 18:00 to 22:00. Afterwards the computer stays fully active until 06:00. Automatic sleep is disabled.

Actions.Text: Enable sleep or shut down after use

Usage.Standby: Sleep disabled; remains at active power
History: 22:00 / last keyboard activity; resident leaves the study.

Appliances.PreInspectionHint: The resident says they finished using the desk much earlier. A notification briefly lights up the otherwise unattended screen.

Appliances.Name: Television
Appliances.Observation: The television is connected to a media receiver.
Appliances.Evidence: The family watches together for two hours, then switches the television off. This routine has stayed the same for several months.
Appliances.PreInspectionHint: The room is quiet now. The remote has been put away with the evening television guide.

Appliances.Name: Microwave
Appliances.Observation: A clock is visible on the display.
Appliances.Evidence: The microwave heats lunch for six minutes each day. The display stays on, but its power draw is much smaller than during heating.

Actions.Text: Stop using it to heat meals

History: 12:30 / a meal is heated for six minutes.
Remaining time / approximately 1 W display draw.

Appliances.PreInspectionHint: Only the clock is lit. A covered meal nearby suggests short reheating rather than prolonged cooking.

Appliances.Name: Coffee maker
Appliances.Observation: A coffee maker sits beside the preparation area.
Appliances.Evidence: The machine brews in the morning and automatically switches off after ten minutes. The warming plate does not run all day.

History: Rest of the day / heating remains off.

Appliances.PreInspectionHint: The switch is off and the plate is cool. A rinsed cup sits on the drying rack.

Appliances.Name: Reading lamp
Appliances.Observation: A small lamp stands beside the reading chair.
Appliances.Evidence: An 8 W LED bulb is used for three occupied hours each evening: 0.024 kWh/day. It is switched off when the resident leaves.

Actions.Text: Remove the light from the room

Appliances.PreInspectionHint: A bookmark rests halfway through a book. The resident describes using this chair for an evening read.

Appliances.Name: Game console
Appliances.Observation: The console is plugged in beside the computer.
Appliances.Evidence: The console is used for an hour on weekends and automatically powers down. Its activity does not match the nightly rise in consumption.

History: Saturday and Sunday / one hour of play each day.

Appliances.PreInspectionHint: The controller is put away. The resident says it mostly comes out for weekend games.

Appliances.Name: Bedroom television
Appliances.Observation: A second television stands on the bedroom dresser.
Appliances.Evidence: The resident watches for an hour before bed. A sleep timer turns it off every night, and the viewing routine has not changed.

Usage.Overnight: Sleep timer switches it off at 22:30
History: 22:30 / sleep timer switches the television off.

Appliances.PreInspectionHint: A sleep-timer option is selected on the remote. The resident mentions watching a little television before bed.

Appliances.Name: Bedside lamp
Appliances.Observation: A small reading lamp stands beside the bed.
Appliances.Evidence: The lamp uses a 5 W LED bulb. It is used for half an hour of reading and is switched off before the resident goes to sleep.

Actions.Text: Keep switching it off after reading
Leave the lamp on until morning
Replace it with a higher-wattage bulb

History: 22:00 / bedside LED switched on for reading.

Appliances.PreInspectionHint: A closed book lies beside the switch. The resident says the light goes out when the book is put down.

Appliances.Name: Living-room floor lamp
Appliances.Observation: A shaded floor lamp stands beside the sofa.
Appliances.Evidence: The lamp has a 7 W LED bulb. The family uses it for three occupied hours each evening, then switches it off when leaving the living room.

Actions.Text: Keep switching it off when the room is empty
Replace the LED with a higher-wattage bulb

Usage.OperatingTime: 3 h/day while the living room is occupied
History: 17:30 / resident turns on the lamp beside the sofa.
20:30 / resident leaves and switches the lamp off.

Appliances.PreInspectionHint: A book and two cups sit by the sofa. The resident describes switching this lamp on when people sit here.

Title: After the guests
Summary: The guests left. Their routines did not.
Brief: Electricity use stayed high after a family visit. Check which routines and device settings were left behind. Resolve three major problems using no more than six inspections.

Appliances.Observation: The refrigerator door is closed and the compressor cycles normally.
Appliances.Evidence: The gasket seals fully. Compressor activity is unchanged and the household has not added any large containers.

Actions.Text: Keep closing the door after use

History: Morning / door opened briefly for breakfast.
Across the day / compressor cycles for about twelve hours.
